title: Augmenting Psychotherapy through Mechanism-Based rTMS in Depression: A Personalized Approach
summary:
In this study, we investigate how different brain networks interact in people with depression. We focus in particular on networks that are involved in thinking and attention, movement, and the processing of visual information.
This brain activity is measured using a specialized magnetic resonance imaging technique, both at rest and while participants perform specific tasks. The aim is to identify different patterns of brain activity in depression and to describe possible subgroups of the disorder.
Afterwards, participants are randomly assigned to one of two treatment groups. In the standard treatment group, a predefined brain region is stimulated. In the personalized treatment group, stimulation is applied to the brain region in which the greatest individual alterations in network function are observed. The treatment consists of a modern form of non-invasive brain stimulation, transcranial magnetic stimulation, which is administered over five consecutive days. This is followed by a six-week course of psychotherapy in the form of cognitive behavioral therapy. The aim of the study is to examine whether brain stimulation can enhance the effects of subsequent psychotherapy, and whether the individually tailored (personalized) treatment is more effective than the standard treatment. In addition, the study investigates whether the altered interaction of brain networks can be normalized through treatment, particularly when stimulation is targeted at the brain regions most affected in each individual.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosis of major depression (based on DSM-5 criteria) (MADRS > 20)
- Written informed consent after comprehensive information about the study
- Clinical condition sufficiently stable so that psychotropic medication can remain unchanged for at least two weeks prior to study entry and throughout the entire study period
Exclusion criteria:
- Current substance use disorder, schizophrenia, or psychotic depression
- Acute suicidality (scores of 4 or 5 on the C-SSRS scale)
- Cognitive impairment (scores below 26 on the MoCA test)
- Cardiac instability
- Contraindications to MRI, e.g. pacemakers or ferromagnetic implants
- Contraindications to CBT (cognitive behavioral therapy)
- Pregnancy and breastfeeding
- Individuals who are hospitalized under a mental health order/act (involuntarily hospitalized patients)
